properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped crypto-browserify stack API surface inside the browserify build output (dist/lightwallet.js, built from this repo's package.json via browserify index.js). The wallet application itself never invokes DES; presence in the shipped bundle is what this inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored crypto stack shipped inside the browserify bundle: crypto-js 3.1.8's TripleDES registration (C_algo.TripleDES = BlockCipher.extend) and crypto-browserify's des-ede3/des-ede3-cbc mode registry. Available in the shipped library (crypto-js is a declared dependency in package.json); no first-party call site in the wallet's own code (lib/) invokes 3DES.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context

Quantum-vulnerable (Shor); migration to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA requires an Ethereum protocol change — observable here, replaceable only ecosystem-wide. App-level use sites lib/signing.js:24/35/65 are bundled into the dist sites.

properties.value: Elliptic 6.4.1's Ed25519 curve definition (defineCurve('ed25519')), a vendored assert, and crypto-browserify's supported-curves table entry (ed25519) — Ed25519 signing is available in the shipped library. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available curve surface in the vendored elliptic library. The app only ever instantiates secp256k1 (lib/keystore.js:17, new EC('secp256k1'), scout 1's object); P-256 is never selected.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: package.json declares Ed25519 capability via tweetnacl 1.0.1 (nacl.sign) and elliptic 6.4.1 (ed25519 curve). No first-party Ed25519 signing found in lib/ — capability present in the shipped libraries, unused by the application.

properties.value: package.json declares X25519 capability via tweetnacl 1.0.1 — the same logical asset as the code-site object ALG-1138d04b (first-party Nacl.box key agreement in lib/encryption.js). Linked so a reader can reference one entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available curve surface in the vendored elliptic + parse-asn1 stack; unused by the app. Meets interim CNSA strength but classical — relevant to a future migration plan only as shipped-surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum's hash — keccak256 is fixed by the protocol (observable, not locally changeable). Not Shor-relevant; its presence is largely positive, with the caveat that hash uses must keep preimage/collision strength under Grover, which 256-bit Keccak does.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 at three layers: BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed (parameters fixed by the BIP39/Ethereum ecosystem), crypto-browserify API surface, and the legacy v1 decrypt path whose 150 iterations are a genuine weakness — but a compat path that must reproduce old vault parameters, superseded by scrypt for new vaults (reported as a finding at lib/keystore.js:340).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 surface available through the bundled crypto-browserify stack. Below CNSA 2.0 (Grover margin 64 bits) but no live application use; the app's own encryption is XSalsa20-Poly1305 with a 256-bit key.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored but live: dist:23347/23351 are the PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 block loop inside bitcore-mnemonic 8.1.1 (BIP39 mnemonic→seed derivation, 2048 iterations), which runs on every vault creation via lib/keystore.js:57 new Mnemonic(mnemonic).toHDPrivateKey(). dist:35968/36360/36618 are crypto-js 3.1.8's HmacSHA256/384/512 helper registrations (library surface). The first-party call site for the BIP39 derivation is reported separately as a finding since the inventory lacks it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 live only in vendored library code: dist:40881/41624 are create-hash wrappers used by hash.js/elliptic internals; dist:61161 hashes the ECDH shared secret in the vendored secp256k1 library's ecdh; dist:8774 is bitcore-lib's Hash.sha256, whose first-party consumer is lib/keystore.js's _concatAndSha256 (seed-entropy mixing in generateRandomSeed, bundle copy). No weakness — SHA-256 is quantum-weakened only by Grover's sqrt speedup.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-async 2.0.1 as shipped: the vendored implementation (dist:60680 module export), the bundle's module map (dist:628), and the package.json:71 dependency declaration. The inventory is missing the first-party call site — lib/keystore.js:312-338 deriveKeyFromPasswordAndSalt invokes ScryptAsync(password, salt, logN=14, r=8, dkLen=32) as the vault's password KDF, with a hardcoded fallback salt — reported separately as a finding with the parameters.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-browserify's supported-ciphers table registering aes-128/192/256-gcm, vendored in the bundle. GCM is available in the shipped crypto stack; no first-party call site uses it — the wallet's authenticated encryption is tweetnacl's XSalsa20-Poly1305. Note for future work: this table is the natural migration target if the legacy crypto-js CBC path is ever replaced.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: package.json declares AES via crypto-js 3.1.8 (also reachable through crypto-browserify in the bundle). First-party AES use exists only in the legacy v1 keystore upgrade path — lib/upgrade.js:14 CryptoJS.AES.decrypt with EvpKDF-MD5 key derivation in CBC mode, reported separately as a finding. crypto-js 3.1.8 is a 2017-era release with no PQ or AEAD guidance.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-512 backs BIP32 HD key derivation, which this wallet exercises for every address it generates. Meets CNSA 2.0 — a positive entry in the inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Library surface for AES-256 in the shipped bundle: crypto-js 3.1.8's default AES configuration (AES.keySize = 256/8 — the helper the legacy upgrade.js path reaches, AES-256-CBC with EvpKDF), crypto-browserify's cipher-table entries (aes-256 in ecb/cbc/cfb/cfb1/cfb8/ofb/ctr/gcm), and asn1.js's OID map. Available in the shipped stack; no first-party call site selects AES-256 through this table. Quantum-safe margin: Grover leaves 128 bits.

First-party call sites live in lib/encryption.js (Nacl.box/secretbox for messages) and lib/keystore.js (Nacl.secretbox encrypting the seed, HD root and per-address private keys — reported as a finding since the deterministic pass missed those source sites). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Positive control: the bundle's randomness for salt, seed entropy and nonces comes from CSPRNGs (crypto.randomBytes via bitcore, tweetnacl's randombytes). The Math.random-based generators are inventoried separately as the weak-PRNG object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Primary crypto provider for the wallet: tweetnacl 1.0.1 (declared in package.json, required in lib/encryption.js and lib/keystore.js, vendored in the bundle). Provides the X25519 box key agreement, XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox (the keystore's data-at-rest cipher), Ed25519 capability, and its internal SHA-512. Version 1.0.1 is a 2017 release with no post-quantum support and no maintained successor in this dependency set — the provider is what decides whether hybrid/PQ groups are even possible here

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js 3.1.8 (declared in package.json, required first-party in lib/keystore.js, lib/upgrade.js, lib/txutils.js, vendored in the bundle). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.4.1 (package.json) — the ECC provider for the wallet's secp256k1 Ethereum keypairs (instantiated first-party at lib/keystore.js:17), and the implementation behind crypto-browserify's createECDH and its ed25519/curve25519 curve definitions in the bundle.
